208.author: Brianmanden
208.task: A player idea: after a kill milestone (for example 100 kills) a wizard unlocks a small companion, such as a little dragon, that follows them, pulls enemy shots toward itself, has its own health, and disappears at 0 health. Nothing like it exists yet (no summons, no taunt or aggro targeting for enemies). It needs a per-player pet that takes player index 0-3, an enemy targeting rule that can prefer it, a health bar, and a say in how a kill-count unlock fits with runs and progression (M3 run structure and M5 meta-progression). It must not make co-op worse: with four players there could be four pets, so shot and particle budgets must hold. It must also fit DESIGN.md's focus on building spells; one option is to make the pet a spell form or relic rather than a separate system. Done when the weekly planning has weighed it against the M3 and M5 designs and either scheduled it or declined it with a reason. Not for M2.
208.title: Idea: summonable pet that draws enemy fire

416.author: peterdk31
416.task: Owner's relic idea for M3, when relics arrive. The Nuke: the wizard has zero mana regeneration, every spellcast spends all current mana however much or little there is, and mana refills completely every X seconds (X to be tuned). Done when it exists as a relic content folder with tests and the spell cost and mana rules support it. Open points for design then: how a cast scales with the mana spent, and the refill interval.
416.title: Relic idea: The Nuke (no mana regen, all-in casts, timed refill)

972.author: hallethebest
972.task: A player on the web build (Preview edition, 1 player) reports poor performance at load, and a heavy frame-rate drop when a beam spell carries several Split cards. Reproduce in the web (Compatibility renderer) build: build a staff with a beam carrier and 2 to 4 Split modifiers, cast it, and measure frame time and the number of projectiles and segments spawned. Find where the cost grows (projectile count, per-beam work, drawing, shader or batch setup) and cut it, keeping the GDScript and native kernels identical and the simulation deterministic. Also check what is slow at startup on the web (shader warmup, resource loading) and trim it if there is something clear. Done when the beam with several Splits stays smooth on the web build, with a benchmark or test covering the case.
972.title: Fix: web slowdown when a beam has several Split cards, and slow load
